description: Convenience and safety-usability improvements (편의개선) in the TUI: (1) add the missing confirmation step for the destructive remote tag deletion action so behavior matches the README's documented safe-default guarantee, and (2) give the commit wizard live feedback on subject length so users stay within the recommended Conventional Commits limit. This feature touches internal/ui/tag.go and internal/ui/commit.go plus a small unit-tested pure helper.
steps: In internal/ui/tag.go, make the 'P' (delete tag on origin) action require a y/N confirmation, mirroring the existing local-delete confirmation. The tagModel already has a confirmDelete bool used for local 'D' delete; add a separate flag (e.g. confirmRemoteDelete bool) so the two prompts do not collide. On 'P', set confirmRemoteDelete=true instead of calling git.DeleteRemoteTag immediately; handle the confirmation in updateList (y/Y -> call git.DeleteRemoteTag(name, "origin"), set successMsg/errMsg, reset flag; any other key -> cancel). Render a distinct confirmation line in viewList (e.g. "원격(origin)에서 태그를 삭제하시겠습니까? <name>") when confirmRemoteDelete is set, following the styling of the existing confirmDelete prompt.
Keep the existing local-delete 'D' confirmation working; ensure only one confirmation can be active at a time and that entering create/show panes clears both flags as appropriate.

In internal/ui/commit.go, add a small pure helper (e.g. func subjectLenHint(n int) (label string, warn bool)) that returns a counter string like "32/50" against a recommended limit of 50 and warn=true once n exceeds 50 (the textinput hard CharLimit stays 72). Render this hint under the subject input in the stepSubject branch of View(): show it dimmed normally and via style.Failure (or style.Label with a caution note) when warn is true. Use utf8.RuneCountInString(m.subject.Value()) for the length so multibyte subjects count correctly.

Add a unit test file internal/ui/commit_helpers_test.go (package ui) covering subjectLenHint: n below, equal to, and above the recommended limit, asserting the label format and the warn boolean transitions at the 50-char boundary.
Run go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... and confirm everything passes.
acceptance_criteria: Pressing 'P' in the tag view shows a confirmation prompt and only deletes the remote tag after 'y'/'Y'; any other key cancels with no remote call.
The local 'D' delete confirmation continues to work independently of the new remote-delete confirmation.
The commit subject step displays a live length counter and switches to a warning style once the subject exceeds the recommended 50 characters.
subjectLenHint is covered by a passing unit test asserting behavior at and across the 50-char boundary.
go build ./..., go vet ./..., and go test ./... all pass.
verification: go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...
findings: internal/ui/tag.go: added confirmRemoteDelete bool alongside existing confirmDelete. 'P' now sets confirmRemoteDelete=true (and clears confirmDelete) instead of calling git.DeleteRemoteTag immediately; confirmation handled in updateList (y/Y deletes on origin, any other key cancels with no remote call). 'D' now also clears confirmRemoteDelete before setting confirmDelete so only one prompt is active at once. Both flags are cleared when entering the create ('c') and show (enter/d) panes. viewList renders a distinct Failure-styled line '원격(origin)에서 태그를 삭제하시겠습니까? <name>' for the remote prompt. internal/ui/commit.go: added const subjectRecommendedLen=50 and pure helper subjectLenHint(n int) (label string, warn bool) returning e.g. '32/50' with warn true only when n > 50 (textinput CharLimit unchanged at 72). stepSubject View() renders the counter under the subject input using utf8.RuneCountInString(m.subject.Value()): style.Dimmed normally, style.Failure with a caution note once warn is true. Added internal/ui/commit_helpers_test.go with TestSubjectLenHint covering below/at/above the 50-char boundary. Verification: go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./..., and go test ./internal/ui/ -run 'SubjectLenHint' -v all pass.
